newsitem.title: CHINA: CHINA GROWTH SEEN AT A HEALTHY 10 PCT IN 1997.
newsitem.headline: CHINA GROWTH SEEN AT A HEALTHY 10 PCT IN 1997.

text.p: China's economy is at its healthiest since the start of the 1990s with growth expected to reach 10 percent this year, fixed asset investment to rise 12.7 percent and inflation to stay below four percent, state economists said.

The latest economic growth cycle, which began about seven years ago, was the first since the 1949 communist takeover to combine a soft landing with high gross domestic product growth, the Xinhua news agency on Wednesday quoted economists at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (CASS) as saying.
"A new cycle of economic growth is beginning as China's economy enters its healthiest period since the 1990s," Xinhua quoted the State Planning Commission as saying.
A recent study by CASS, China's premier think-tank, and the State Statistical Bureau forecast GDP growth of 10 percent this year.
It forecast investment in fixed assets to rise by 12.7 percent while benchmark retail price inflation would be four percent or less.

The retail price index rose by 0.6 percent in July year-on-year, the lowest rate since the end of the 1980s, the State Planning Commission said on Tuesday. Consumer price inflation rose an annual 2.7 percent for July.

Economists attributed the healthy economic picture in part to an appropriately tight monetary policy and introduction of more flexible interest and exchange rates as well as more stable prices following several bumper harvests.

Expenditure as well as investment and exports -- the three major forces in the economy -- were now on a strong footing, Xinhua quoted Xu Hongyuan, an associate research fellow of the State Information Centre, as saying.
Xu said the economic boom would be useful in solving micro-economic problems, such as low efficiency in the state-owned sector and an unbalanced industrial structure.
He stressed the need for the government to maintain a "moderately tight" monetary policy with increased flexibility.
